title: DR Congo river boat under quarantine for Ebola after five deaths
facts: Congolese authorities screened 255 passengers on a boat on the Congo River for Ebola and cholera.
The intercepted Congo River boat is the Yingfeng 2, operated by a Chinese company.
The Yingfeng 2 was halted near Bende Bende port, approximately 65 kilometers upstream from Kinshasa.
Roger Kamba serves as the Health Minister of the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Five people from the vessel died, including three adults, a three-year-old child, and a newborn.
The Yingfeng 2 departed from Mongala Province in north-western DR Congo.
The vessel traveled more than 1,700 kilometers downstream toward Kinshasa before being intercepted.
Teams from the World Health Organization boarded the Yingfeng 2 to set up a mobile testing laboratory.
The current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo was declared on May 15.
The ongoing Ebola outbreak in DR Congo is caused by the Bundibugyo species of the virus.
Human clinical trials for a Bundibugyo Ebola vaccine are currently underway in the United Kingdom.
Official figures reported 3,973 confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has caused 1,801 deaths.
Authorities placed more than 17,000 people under monitoring for contact with Ebola cases across five provinces.
Congolese health authorities recorded 776 recoveries from Ebola during the current outbreak.
